la:verb:aro.gloss: to plough, till; to cultivate land, farm; to acquire by tillage
senses: to plough, till; to cultivate land, farm; to acquire by tillage
to draw furrows over the body, wrinkle
la:verb:aro.html:
ăro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
cf. ἀρόω = to plough, to till; ἄροτρον = aratrum; ἄροτος, ἄρουρα = arvum, = Welsh ar; ἀροτήρ = arator; armentum; Goth. arjan = to plough; O. H. Germ. aran = to ear
,
to plough, to till.
Lit.
Absol.: arare mavelim quam sic amare,: in fundo Fodere aut arare,: si quidem L. Quinctio Cincinnato aranti nuntiatum est etc.,: bene et tempestive arare,; : bos est enectus arando,: die septimo cessabis arare et metere,; ; .—
With acc.: arare terram,; ; cf. ; : ager non semel aratus, sed novatus et iteratus,: cum terra araretur et sulcus altius esset impressus,: vallem arari,: campum arare,: olivetum,: Capuam,: Campaniam, et saep.—
Trop
Of a ship, to plough: aequor. ; so Heins.; ; : aquas, (cf.: sulcare aquas,).—
Of age, to draw furrows over the body, i. e. to wrinkle: jam venient rugae, quae tibi corpus arent,.—
In mal. part.: fundum alienum,; so —
Prov.: arare litus, for to bestow useless labor: non profecturis litora bobus aras,; so ; cf. .—
In a more extended sense.
To cultivate land, and absol. to pursue agriculture, to live by husbandry (cf. agricola and arator): quae homines arant, navigant, aedificant, virtuti omnia parent, i. e. in agriculturā, navigatione, etc., omnia ex virtute animi pendent, Corte' arat Falerni mille fundi jugera, : cives Romani, qui arant in Siciliā,.—
To gain by agriculture, to acquire by tillage: decem medimna ex jugero arare, (where, Zumpt, from conjecture, has received exarare into the text; so B. and K.).

la:noun:aroma.html:
ărōma, ătis, n. (dat. and
abl. plur. aromatibus, also aromatis, ; v. Neue, Formenl. I. p. 291), = ἄρωμα, a spice; in sing., ; Prud. στεφ. 8, 72; ; in plur., spices (so only in Vulg.), ; ; ; ; et saepe.

ăros, i, f., also ăron or ărum, i, n., = ἄρον,
